content.text:
I'd go with Harel's **"מניות"** track. Out of everything on the page it went up the most: "24.04%" over 3 years and "14.64%" over 5. The "עוקב מדד S&P 500" track, the one my friends at work talk about, only shows "13.7%" and "11.92%". The fees are basically the same, 0.55% against 0.56%, so the bigger return decided it. "מניות" is also a big fund, "7.3 מיליארד ₪", so lots of people are in it. I'm fairly sure, not totally. If I lose my nerve, the S&P one is my fallback.

**How it went**
- **First screen:** I saw the big heading "הראל" and the "קופת גמל להשקעה 16" button, which was already highlighted, so I knew I was in the right place. Under it the fees go "מ־0.54% עד 0.61%".
- **The table:** I scrolled through it and read the right side (track name), then the fee, then the return. The first rows, "אג"ח סחיר", "אשראי ואג"ח" and "כספי (שקלי)", have no money in shares and low or no returns, so I skipped them. "כללי" shows 13.5%. "מניות" has the big 24.04%. "S&P 500" was the name I knew.
- **Rows with no number:** A lot of rows just say "פחות מ־3 שנים" where the return should be. I can't compare those, so I ignored them.
- **Skipped:**
  - The bit at the bottom of the table about the legal fee limit and "PF-10"
  - The grey line under the table
  - All the "מה כתוב במסמכים של הראל" folds
  - The search box and the footer
  - The "מה זה קופת גמל להשקעה" link
- **Words I didn't get:**
  - The "מט"ח" percent next to "מניות" in each row (25% for "מניות", 99% for S&P). I guessed it means how much is in foreign stuff.
  - "קופה" with a number like 8522
  - The "ההפקדות 0%" line under the fee
  - "אג"ח סחיר"
  - "סחיר" in "מניות סחיר", and why that's a separate track from "מניות"
- **Where I hesitated:** I'm torn between "מניות" and "S&P 500", since the S&P is what everyone says to buy. A few rows were also cut off between my screenshots, and the list ended at row 16 without me seeing all of them, so maybe I missed one.
- **What bothered me:**
  - The fee is only shown as a percent, so I have no idea what it costs me in shekels on 30,000.
  - There's no button saying how to actually open the fund, so I don't know what the first step is.
